# HTTP API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-api-reference.mjs from src/app/**/route.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every route handler of phis, derived from the code. **Access** names what the handler checks before it
answers: `internal token` is the Site token (`x-phis-token`) with internal scope, `API token` accepts a
public or internal token, and `session` is the visitor's Site session with the access policy the guard
passes (see [AUTHORIZATION.md](../AUTHORIZATION.md)). A route with no access entry performs its own checks
or none; read its source. Request and response shapes are not listed; the source is linked per route.

189 routes.

## `/api/operator`

| Method | Address | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

## `/api/site`

Site administration, CMS, media and support API. A Site's `/api/site` proxy forwards the visitor's session.

| Method | Address | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | [`/api/site/account/addresses`](../src/app/api/site/account/addresses/route.ts) | session, `authenticated` (requireSiteAuthenticatedApiContext) | The signed-in person's current addresses on this Site (neither `Superseded` nor `Removed`), oldest first: `{ items: PhisSiteAddress[] }` (`@phis/contracts/users`). The address book is the Site's, so another Site shows its own. |
| POST | [`/api/site/account/addresses`](../src/app/api/site/account/addresses/route.ts) | session, `authenticated` (requireSiteAuthenticatedApiContext) | Writes an address for the signed-in person: `{ address: PhisSiteAddressInput, flags }`, `flags` of `Billing`, `Shipping`, `DefaultBilling`, `DefaultShipping` (at least one purpose, a default only with its purpose). Answers `201` with the `PhisSiteAddress`; one equal in every part to a current one is that one, given the purposes and defaults besides, and a default moves from the address that held it. `400` for an address or flags that are refused. |
| PUT | [`/api/site/account/addresses/{id}`](../src/app/api/site/account/addresses/[id]/route.ts) | session, `authenticated` (requireSiteAuthenticatedApiContext) | Changes one of the signed-in person's current addresses: `{ address, flags }` as for `POST`, written as a new version that replaces it (the old one becomes `Superseded`). Answers the new `PhisSiteAddress`, or the current one equal to it; `404` for an id that is no current address of theirs on this Site. |
| DELETE | [`/api/site/account/addresses/{id}`](../src/app/api/site/account/addresses/[id]/route.ts) | session, `authenticated` (requireSiteAuthenticatedApiContext) | Removes one of the signed-in person's current addresses and the versions it followed. Answers `{ outcome: "deleted" }` where no Add-on was ever handed it, and `{ outcome: "removed" }` where one was: it stays, `Removed`, for the records that may point at it, and is gone from the account. `404` for an id that is no current address of theirs on this Site. |

| POST | [`/api/site/admin/users`](../src/app/api/site/admin/users/route.ts) | session, `site-admin` (requireSiteAdminOnlyApiContext) |  |

| GET | [`/api/site/admin/users-access`](../src/app/api/site/admin/users-access/route.ts) | session, `site-admin` (requireSiteAdminOnlyApiContext) | What this Site lets Add-ons read of people with nobody acting (`users:v1` background access), and how long it keeps the access log: `{ retentionDays, addons: [{ addonId, fields, background, granted, effective, awaiting, grantedAt, grantedByUserId }] }`, one row per installed Add-on requiring `users:v1`. `fields` is what the manifest reads at all, `background` what it asks to read with nobody acting, `granted` the Site's grant, `effective` what of it counts (granted and still asked), `awaiting` what is asked and not granted. Site Admin only. |
| PUT | [`/api/site/admin/users-access/{addonId}`](../src/app/api/site/admin/users-access/[addonId]/route.ts) | session, `site-admin` (requireSiteAdminOnlyApiContext) | Grants an Add-on background access to `users:v1` on this Site: `{ fields }`, a non-empty part of what its manifest asks in `users.background`, which becomes the whole grant. Answers the Add-on's row as `GET /api/site/admin/users-access` lists it. `404` for an Add-on that is not installed or does not require `users:v1`, `400` for fields it does not ask, `409` for one not yet reconciled into the registry. The id is one percent-encoded path segment. Site Admin only; the grant names who gave it. |
| DELETE | [`/api/site/admin/users-access/{addonId}`](../src/app/api/site/admin/users-access/[addonId]/route.ts) | session, `site-admin` (requireSiteAdminOnlyApiContext) | Withdraws an Add-on's background access to `users:v1` on this Site, installed or not: `{ revoked }`, false where there was no grant. Site Admin only. |
| GET | [`/api/site/admin/users-access/log`](../src/app/api/site/admin/users-access/log/route.ts) | session, `site-admin` (requireSiteAdminOnlyApiContext) | This Site's `users:v1` access log, newest first, a page at a time (`page`, `pageSize` up to 100, 25 by default), narrowed with `subject` (an entitlement subject among those named) and `addonId`: `{ items: [{ at, addonId, actor: { userId, displayName } \| null, road, operation, subjects, addressIds, fields }] }`. `road` is `staff`, `self`, `background` or `checkout`; `operation` `describe`, `addresses`, `createAddress`, `fileOf` or `customerFile` (Core's own, `addonId` `@phis/server`); `fields` the `users:v1` fields the answer carried. Site Admin only. |
| PUT | [`/api/site/admin/users-access/retention`](../src/app/api/site/admin/users-access/retention/route.ts) | session, `site-admin` (requireSiteAdminOnlyApiContext) | How many days this Site keeps its `users:v1` access log: `{ days }`, a whole number from 1 to 3650 (`sites.users_access_log_days`, also `phis site set --users-access-log-days`). Answers `{ retentionDays }`; the Core job `users-access-log.prune` forgets older entries on its next run. Site Admin only. |

| GET | [`/api/site/members`](../src/app/api/site/members/route.ts) | session, `accounting-or-support` (requireSiteAccountingOrSupportApiContext) | The Site's members, for a picker that names a person by user id (a licence granted on somebody's behalf): `q` matched on the name and the e-mail addresses, and a `q` that is a telephone number on the digits of the business telephone and the mobile number, `page` and `pageSize` (at most 50). Answers `{ items }`, each `{ userId, displayName }`, ordered by name -- the name the person is shown under, or `#<id>` without one, never the address or number that may have been searched by. For the staff who act on a member's behalf, the holders of the Site access `accounting` or `support`, which Core asks before it names a member to an Add-on (`subjectForUser`); the Site's user list is the Site Admin's and the group candidates are a group Manager's. |
| GET | [`/api/site/members/{userId}/file`](../src/app/api/site/members/[userId]/file/route.ts) | session, `accounting-or-support` (requireSiteAccountingOrSupportApiContext) | Staff's customer file on one member of the Site: `{ person: { userId, displayName, name?, email?, phone?, addresses? }, fileThreadId, threads }`. The person's fields follow the staff road of `users:v1` -- the Site access `support` reads name, e-mail and telephone, `accounting` (and a Site Admin) also the Site's current addresses -- and the read is written to the access log. `fileThreadId` is the person's file (`PhisThreadKind.File`), opened on first asking; `threads` are the inbox rows of the threads the person takes part in that the actor may see, a page at a time (`page`, `pageSize` up to 100). For the holders of `accounting` or `support`; `403` for the actor's own file, which nobody reaches, `404` for a user who is no member of the Site. |
| GET | [`/api/site/products`](../src/app/api/site/products/route.ts) | session, `accounting` (requireSiteAccountingApiContext) | The Site's product directory, a page at a time: `supplier` (an Add-on id), `state` (a comma-separated list of draft, active, withdrawn, locked; absent: every state), `pendingTerms` (true: only products waiting for the operator's release, false: only those that are not), `q` (a part of the title or the id), `page` and `pageSize`. Answers `{ rows, total, page, pageSize }`, each row the product's id, supplier, publisher, title, summary, type, state, sale, referralUrl, free, accountRequired, counted, parts, released, pendingTerms, imagePath, iconPath, imageListPath, iconListPath and version. imageListPath and iconListPath are the picture's and the icon's `icon` variant (64 x 64, fitted whole on a transparent ground) for a list that shows them small, with the delivery revision and the variant version, null without one or for an Asset that is no image. |
| POST | [`/api/site/products/{id}/lock`](../src/app/api/site/products/[id]/lock/route.ts) | session, `accounting` (requireSiteAccountingApiContext) | Locks a product, the Site operator's alone: no entry for it counts while it is locked, as `phis product lock` does. Answers `{ outcome, product }`, `product` in the shape of a `GET /api/site/products` row, outcome `locked` or `unchanged`. The id is one path segment, percent-encoded (`@`, `/` and `:` are in every id). |
| POST | [`/api/site/products/{id}/release`](../src/app/api/site/products/[id]/release/route.ts) | session, `accounting` (requireSiteAccountingApiContext) | Releases a publisher's product, the first time or its pending terms, as `phis product release` does. The body is empty or `{ expectedVersion }`, the version whose terms the operator read. Answers `{ outcome, product }`, `product` in the shape of a `GET /api/site/products` row, outcome `released`, `applied` or `unchanged`; `409` for the Site's own product, which needs no release, and for a product whose version is no longer `expectedVersion`. The id is one path segment, percent-encoded (`@`, `/` and `:` are in every id). |
| POST | [`/api/site/products/{id}/unlock`](../src/app/api/site/products/[id]/unlock/route.ts) | session, `accounting` (requireSiteAccountingApiContext) | Unlocks a locked product, which becomes `withdrawn` -- the state before the lock is not kept -- as `phis product unlock` does. Answers `{ outcome, product }`, `product` in the shape of a `GET /api/site/products` row, outcome `unlocked` or `unchanged`. The id is one path segment, percent-encoded (`@`, `/` and `:` are in every id). |
